script: I got banned for a harmless comment—this policy ruined my life.. I was scrolling through the comment thread, eyes already glazing over the endless stream of "I am the asshole" posts, when I noticed the same old pattern: people were spamming political arguments, turning every discussion into a mini debate hall. The sub was drowning in ideology, not in the juicy Am I the jerk drama we love. I knew I had to step in. I drafted a new rule, sharper than the last one, and posted it straight to the top. I wrote: "New rule: no political trolling." Then I got into the details, because I am the best moderator in the world and I don't let anything slip. I told everyone that any post whose main focus is politics—no matter how passionate or clever—would be removed, and the account would get a ban. I added a clause for genuine posts that accidentally trigger a flood of rule‑violating comments: they'd be deleted, but no ban. I was like, "If you're just talking about politics, stay in the right sub, okay?" I also clarified that a passing mention of a politician or a quick nod to a policy is fine, but if the whole judgment hinges on whether you agree with a political stance, that's a no‑no. And if someone's trying to push an agenda, that's a hard "no." I reminded everyone that we're not a politics sub; there are better places for that. And I left an open line: "If you have any questions, hit us up in modmail." Because I am always here to drop some tea and keep the vibe smooth. That's it. I hit publish, watched the new rule sit there like a fresh coat of paint, and hoped it would keep the Am I the jerk playground free from the endless political circus. The rest? Well, that's just how it goes.
